The graph displays the daily number of new COVID-19 cases and news reports over time. The horizontal axis represents dates from July 1, 2022, to August 26, 2022, labeled in a sequence of dates, with no specific interval between each date label. The vertical axis on the left side represents the number of people, ranging from 0 to 1,800,000, with a linear scale and numerical tick marks at intervals of 200,000. The vertical axis on the right side represents an unspecified count, ranging from 0 to 6,000, also with a linear scale and numerical tick marks at intervals of 1,000.

The graph features two types of bars: blue bars representing "the global confirmed cases" and a line representing "related COVID-19 news". The blue bars vary in height, with the shortest bar approximately at 600,000 and the tallest bar reaching nearly 1,700,000. There is no clear consistent trend in the heights of the blue bars throughout the graph. The line fluctuates, with values ranging from around 1,000 to 4,000. 

There is no specific order or grouping of the bars, and no bar is visually emphasized. The graph presents a visual representation of the daily number of new COVID-19 cases and news reports over a specific period, without any apparent grouping, stacking, or sorting of the bars.
